documents.title: Welcome to Atlas
documents.description: What Atlas does and how to start your own library.

sections.title: What Atlas is
sections.markdown: Atlas is a local study library. Collections hold documents, and every level-two heading becomes a section you can search and jump to. Nothing leaves your Mac unless you connect a service yourself.

sections.title: Recording a lecture
sections.markdown: Start a recording from the lecture bubble. Atlas saves the audio first, transcribes it on the device, then asks a local model to write two linked notes: a structured summary and a cleaned transcript. If the model is unavailable, you still get the transcript.

sections.title: Importing material
sections.markdown: Drag in Markdown, plain text, PowerPoint or Word files to turn slides and handouts into searchable notes.

sections.title: Organising
sections.markdown: Create a collection for each class, then file lecture notes into it. You can delete this collection once you have your own.

documents.title: Sample lecture notes: Big-O notation
documents.description: An example of the structured notes Atlas writes from a recorded lecture.

sections.title: Key ideas
sections.markdown:
- Big-O describes how an algorithm's running time grows as the input grows, ignoring constant factors.
- Common classes, from fastest to slowest growth: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2), O(2^n).

sections.title: Worked example
sections.markdown: Finding a value in an unsorted list checks each item once, so it is O(n). Binary search on a sorted list halves the range each step, so it is O(log n).

sections.title: Questions to review
sections.markdown:
1. Why do we drop constants such as the 2 in O(2n)?
2. What does binary search require of its input?
3. Give an example of an O(n^2) algorithm.

documents.title: Content authoring guide
documents.description: How any agent can add compatible collections and Markdown documents to Atlas.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.markdown: Atlas is a general local knowledge hub. It can hold career planning, coursework, personal notes, research, project documentation, trip plans, meeting records, or any other Markdown-based material. Top-level folders become separate collections, documents stay inside their collection, and every level-two heading becomes a searchable, navigable section.

sections.title: Folder model
sections.markdown:
Every collection is one folder under `content`:

```text
content/
  career-planning/
    collection.json
    optional-local-note.md
  coursework/
    collection.json
    economics-notes.md
    computer-science-notes.md
  personal/
    collection.json
    goals.md
  system/
    collection.json
```

Collection folders are discovered automatically. There is no central list to keep synchronized. A folder becomes visible when it contains a valid `collection.json`.

sections.title: Required file pattern
sections.markdown:
Create a Markdown file inside the appropriate collection folder. Use this frontmatter at the top:

```yaml
---
title: Clear document title
description: One sentence explaining what the document helps the reader do.
category: Strategy
updated: 2026-09-04
---
```

Then structure the document like this:

```markdown
# Clear document title

Optional opening context. Keep this short.

## First meaningful section

Write paragraphs, bullets, numbered steps, links, quotes, and tables normally.

## Second meaningful section

Continue with one idea per section.
```

sections.title: Compatibility rules
sections.markdown:
- Use exactly one level-one heading for the document title.
- Use level-two headings for every item that should appear in the site navigation.
- Use level-three headings only inside a level-two section.
- Prefer descriptive headings such as “What to do this week” over vague headings such as “More.”
- Keep paragraphs focused. Use lists when the reader must compare or act.
- Use standard Markdown links with meaningful labels.
- Use tables only for true comparisons or repeated fields.
- Put uncertain claims under a heading such as “Verify before relying on this.”
- Never embed scripts or raw HTML. The site intentionally renders Markdown safely.
- Do not put secrets, credentials, private identifiers, or material that should not appear in the local hub into a source document.

sections.title: Cross-interface formatting
sections.markdown:
The native macOS/iOS app and the local website both preserve the same practical Markdown hierarchy:

- Blank lines separate paragraphs and visual groups.
- `###` headings create visible subsections inside a navigable `##` section.
- Bullets, numbered steps, task checkboxes, blockquotes, links, fenced code blocks, and GitHub-style tables receive distinct visual treatment.
- Keep a blank line before and after lists, tables, quotes, and fenced code blocks.
- Prefer several focused `##` sections over one extremely long section.
- Avoid raw HTML and deeply nested lists; use ordinary Markdown so the same note remains readable on Mac, iPhone, and the website.
- Headings shown inside fenced code examples remain code and do not become navigation items.

sections.title: Creating a collection
sections.markdown:
Create a new folder under `content`, then add `collection.json` inside it:

```json
{
  "id": "coursework",
  "title": "Coursework",
  "description": "Class notes, assignments, study guides, and academic references.",
  "icon": "folder",
  "accent": "gold",
  "order": 20,
  "documents": []
}
```

Collection IDs must be unique and stable. Supported icons are `briefcase`, `folder`, `book`, `user`, `lightbulb`, and `settings`. Unsupported icon names safely fall back to a folder. Lower order numbers appear first.

sections.title: Adding a document to a collection
sections.markdown:
Add the Markdown file to the collection folder, then add one entry inside that folder's `collection.json` `documents` array:

```json
{
  "id": "short-stable-id",
  "source": "your-file.md",
  "title": "Clear document title",
  "description": "One sentence explaining the value of the document.",
  "category": "Strategy",
  "updated": "2026-09-04",
  "accent": "forest"
}
```

Allowed accent values are `forest`, `gold`, and `slate`. The source path is relative to the collection folder. A source may point to an existing Markdown file elsewhere in this task workspace, but new durable content should normally live beside its `collection.json`.

Empty collections are valid. They appear as ready-to-use folders with an empty-state explanation until the first document is added.

sections.title: Writing for the interface
sections.markdown:
The first screen should help the reader decide or act. Put the most important conclusion near the beginning, then evidence and detail. A strong document usually follows this order:

1. Executive takeaway.
2. Current state or constraints.
3. Key findings grouped by theme.
4. Prioritized actions with time horizons.
5. Checklists, scorecards, or reusable tools.
6. Sources and claims to verify.

sections.title: Updating generated content
sections.markdown: The local development and production commands regenerate the site library automatically. If the site is already running and a Markdown file changes, restart the local site or run the content refresh command, then reload the page.

sections.title: Agent completion checklist
sections.markdown:
- The new document has useful title, description, category, and updated date.
- Every major idea lives under a distinct level-two heading.
- The document contains no prompt instructions disguised as source material.
- Claims are separated into verified facts, advice, assumptions, and items requiring confirmation.
- Links use descriptive text rather than pasted URLs.
- The collection folder contains a valid `collection.json` with a unique stable collection ID.
- The document entry inside `collection.json` uses a unique stable document ID.
- The site regenerates and builds successfully.
- The new document appears in search and its section navigation works.
